assessments.reasoning: Five contiguous captures cover bytes [0,73836) of SPDX’s commit-pinned json/details/GPL-2.0-only.json, reported SHA-256 e8d048eeb2eb042ec0437ca2b7b360baef48eaec7fb9e4e9b792aaf9ed33794b. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 3 gives the exact licenseId, name, comment and version-2-only header. Its seeAlso entries cite GNU’s standalone HTML and text, OSI and OpenJDK. These are leads with different authority and scope.

The SPDX repository’s annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the revision in the detail URL. Capture 9c9c8acc5979433a89fc09b221f96ebf records the GitHub API response. The tag is unsigned. Its evidentiary role is the repository’s release-to-commit mapping.

The digest-pinned GNU text identifies version 2. Section 0 ties application to the copyright holder’s notice, and §9 conditions its numbered-version later election on the Program specifying “any later version.” The publisher’s appendix illustrates the later option. This source supplies edition and notice context. SPDX supplies the identifier.

limitations: The shared subject and edition identify the underlying GPL document. The version-2-only restriction appears in the claim statement but is absent from its structured conditions. Reading the key as an unconditional assignment to that edition would lose the distinction between the two claims.

SPDX matching templates and example headers guide identification. A real file’s applicable grant and any modifications require project evidence. A shared text match or a project-level LICENSE reference cannot establish the election for all files.
reasoning: SPDX 3.29.0 lists GPL-2.0-only for code whose applicable notice specifies version 2 alone. The decisive evidence is the combination of licenseId, licenseComments and standardLicenseHeader. The apparent wording inconsistency is within the generated representation: its standard header ends the election at “version 2.” while its licenseText appendix illustrates “any later version.” SPDX explicitly explains the difference. The candidate’s “granting use” is a paraphrase of the version election. The actual notice speaks of redistribution and modification.
